title: Endogenous protein interactomes resolved through immunoprecipitation-coupled quantitative proteomics in cell lines
protocol: Incubate 50 μL packed volume of Protein G Sepharose beads with 5–50 μg of antibody or control IgG in phosphate buffered saline (PBS, pH7.2) for 16 hours on a rotator at 20 rpm at 4°C to conjugate antibodies to the beads.
Centrifuge tubes at 1,000 × g for 1 minute and remove supernatant.
Wash beads three times with 1 mL of 0.2 M triethanolamine diluted in ddH2O and pH adjusted to 8.2 with HCl.
Resuspend beads in 1 mL of 0.2 M triethanolamine.
Centrifuge tubes at 1,000 × g for 1 minute and remove supernatant.
Repeat washing steps three times.
Resuspend beads in 1 mL of a freshly made solution containing 20 mM dimethyl pimelimidate-2HCl and 0.2 M triethanolamine, pH 8.2.
Mix tubes on rotator at 20 rpm for 60 min at 20°C–22°C to ensure beads remain in suspension.
Centrifuge tubes at 1,000 × g for 1 min and remove the supernatant.
Resuspend beads in 1 mL of 0.2 M ethanolamine pH 8.0.
Centrifuge tubes at 1,000 × g for 1 min and remove the supernatant.
Resuspend beads in 1 mL of 0.2 M ethanolamine pH 8.0 and mix tubes on rotator at 20 rpm for 30 min at 20°C–22°C.
Centrifuge tubes at 1,000 × g for 1 min and remove the supernatant.
Wash beads twice with 1 mL of PBS.
Store the beads in PBS at 4°C and use within 48 hours.
Isolate protein lysates from cell lines by culturing approximately 3 x 10^6 cells for each IP, adjusting number as necessary based on specific cell line requirements.
Remove media from cells and wash with 10 mL of PBS.
Add 2 mL of pre-warmed (37°C) 0.05% Trypsin-EDTA Tissue Culture Solution to detach the cells.
Incubate at 37°C until cells detach, approximately 5 minutes.
Neutralize Trypsin by adding 5 mL of culture media and transfer cells to a 10 mL centrifuge tube.
Centrifuge cells at 300 × g for 5 min.
Remove supernatant and resuspend cells in 10 mL of PBS.
Centrifuge cells at 300 × g for 5 min.
Remove supernatant and resuspend cells in 1 mL of PBS.
Transfer cells to a 1.6 mL screw-capped Eppendorf.
Centrifuge at 300 × g for 5 min.
Remove supernatant.
Resuspend and lyse cells in 250 μL ice cold Protein Lysis Buffer.
Sonicate solution using a Vibra-Cell VCX 130 sonicator fitted with a 3 mm tip set at 30% amplitude for 12 s.
Return tube to ice for 2 min.
Repeat sonication for 5 s.
Add 250 μL lysis buffer to each tube following sonication.
Centrifuge at 15,000 × g at 4°C for 15 min.
Transfer supernatants to new 1.6 mL screw-capped Eppendorf tubes.
Quantitate protein concentration using a Bicinchoninic Assay kit as per manufacturer’s instructions.
Split each lysate into two samples, an Input sample and an IP sample.
Add 600 μg of lysate (of variable volume based on protein concentration) to lysis buffer to make a final volume of 500 μL for the IP Sample.
Store the remaining lysate as the Input Sample at −80°C.
Prewash 50 μL packed volume of Protein G Sepharose beads with 1 mL Protein Lysis Buffer at 4°C.
Centrifuge the beads at 1,000 × g for 5 min at 4°C and remove the supernatant.
Add 500 μL IP sample to the prewashed beads and incubate at 4°C for 15 min on a rotator at 20 rpm.
Centrifuge the tubes at 1,000 × g for 5 min. The supernatant is now considered a ‘pre-cleared’ IP sample.
Remove the supernatant from pre-prepared antibody or control IgG-conjugated Protein G Sepharose beads.
Add 500 μL of the pre-cleared IP Sample to the beads and incubate on a rotator at 4°C for 16 h.
Prepare Microspin G50 columns by removing pre-packed Sephadex G-50 beads, attaching fixed snap-off plugs from the column tips, and adding 1 mL low-salt wash buffer.
Centrifuge the columns using a capsulefuge and discard the flow-through.
Transfer each IP Sample (lysates and beads) to MicroSpin G50 columns. Centrifuge and discard the flow-through.
Wash the IP beads in the Microspin G50 column three times with 500 μL Protein Lysis Buffer. Centrifuge after each wash, discarding the flow-through.
Add 500 μL of IP Low Salt Wash Buffer.
Centrifuge using a low speed capsulefuge.
Discard the flow-through.
Elute the IP sample.
Close one end of each column with a snap-off plug.
Add 40 μL IP Elution Buffer into each column.
Incubate at 20°C–22°C for 7 min.
Unplug ends of the columns and place them in a collection tube containing 0.3 μL 100 mM Dithiothreitol (DTT).
Spin using a low speed capsulefuge to collect eluate.
Repeat steps i-iv using 20 μL IP Elution Buffer.
Pool the two elutions for each IP-Sample from step and store at −80°C.
Add 20 mM Tris-HCl (pH 7.5) to create aliquot volumes of 7.5 μL each.
Add 2.5 μL of 4× Laemmli Buffer to the aliquots and mix by pipetting.
Incubate aliquots at 95°C for 5 min and then place on ice.
Assemble the XCell SureLock Mini-Cell system with a pre-cast NuPAGE 3%–8% Tris-Acetate 1.5 mm Mini Protein Gel as per manufacturers' instructions.
Add 250 μL of NuPAGE Antioxidant to 250 mL of 1× NuPAGE Tris-Acetate SDS Running Buffer and pour into the inner buffer chamber.
Fill the outer chamber with 1× NuPAGE Tris-Acetate SDS Running Buffer to a level approximately 3 cm above the bottom of the gel.
Remove gel comb and wash wells using a 1 mL pipette tip.
Load all 10 μL of the Input and IP Sample aliquots using gel loading tips.
Load 5 μL of Precision Plus Protein Dual Color Standards (add 5 μL 1× Laemmli Buffer) in flanking wells.
Run samples at 100 V for 2 hours.
Transfer proteins to a nitrocellulose membrane.
Soak the precast gel in cold Western Transfer Buffer for 5 min.
Pre-soak 'cut-to-gel' sized nitrocellulose membrane (BioTrace NT) and two Whatman filter papers (3 mm CHR) in cold Western Transfer Buffer.
Place the nitrocellulose membrane on top of the gel, followed by two Whatman filter papers and blotting pads.
Assemble the transfer blot ‘sandwich’ in the XCell II Blot Module.
Fill the transfer chamber with cold Western Transfer Buffer.
Transfer at 15 V for 16 h in a 4°C cold room.
Incubate the nitrocellulose membrane with Ponceau S Stain for 5 min.
Wash excess stain using TBST repeatedly.
Remove remaining protein-bound Ponceau S Stain using repeated washes with TBST.
Conduct western immunoblotting.
Block the nitrocellulose membrane with TBST containing 10% skim milk for 1 h.
Incubate the membrane for 16 h at 4°C in TBST containing primary antibody and 2% skim milk.
Wash the membrane with TBST buffer 3× 10 min each wash.
Incubate the membrane at room temperature for 2 h with TBST containing 2% skim milk and HRP-conjugated secondary antibodies.
Wash the membrane with TBST buffer 3× 10 min each wash.
Remove TBST using a Whatman filter.
Incubate the membrane with Clarity Western ECL Substrate reagent for 2 min.
Prepare a 35 μL aliquot of each IP sample for SDS-PAGE by adding 12 μL of 4× Laemmli Buffer.
Incubate the samples at 95°C and then return to ice.
Prepare the SDS-PAGE apparatus as per step 4.
Load a single IP sample across multiple wells if necessary.
Run the gel at 200 V for 10 minutes.
Conduct a Coomassie stain of the proteins.
Carefully remove precast gels from cassettes.
Wash gels with Fixing Solution for 5 minutes.
Remove Fixing Solution and incubate gels with Coomassie Stain for 16 hours.
Discard Coomassie Stain and remove any remaining traces using three 5-minute incubations in Coomassie Wash Solution with slight agitation.
Rehydrate the gel by incubating in Gel Rehydration Solution for 1 hour.
Immerse the entire gel in ddH2O water for 1 hour, changing the water every 20 minutes.
Excise all gel regions containing protein and place them on a clean surface.
Use a scalpel to excise gel regions containing protein of each sample.
Pool multiple wells of the same sample together where relevant.
Dice gel regions further into smaller pieces of 1 × 1 mm.
Place diced gel pieces inside Protein LoBind microcentrifuge tubes.
Centrifuge tubes at 1,000 × g for 1 minute to collect gel pieces in the bottom of the tube.
Wash gel pieces with acetonitrile by adding 500 μL of acetonitrile (LC-MS grade) and incubating for 10 minutes at 20°C–22°C.
Pulse vortex tubes during washing to separate gel pieces.
Centrifuge at 1,000 × g for 1 min.
Discard the supernatant.
Add 30 μL of the 10 mM DTT Solution in TEAB to each sample.
Incubate the samples in a heating block/incubator for 30 min at 56°C.
Cool the sample tubes to 20°C–22°C.
Wash gel pieces with acetonitrile.
Add 500 μL of acetonitrile (LC-MS grade) to each sample.
Incubate tubes for 10 min at 20°C–22°C.
Centrifuge tubes at 1,000 × g for 1 min.
Discard the supernatant.
Add 30 μL of 55 mM iodoacetamide (IAM) in TEAB solution to the sample.
Incubate the samples in the dark at 20°C–22°C for 20 min.
Wash gel pieces with acetonitrile.
Add 500 μL of acetonitrile (LC-MS grade) to each sample.
Incubate tubes for 10 min at 20°C–22°C.
Centrifuge tubes at 1,000 × g for 1 min.
Discard the supernatant.
De-stain the gel pieces.
Add 500 μL of Destaining Solution to each sample.
Incubate the samples at 20°C–22°C for 20 min.
Discard the supernatant.
Wash gel pieces with acetonitrile.
Add 500 μL of acetonitrile to each sample.
Vortex samples for 10 s.
Incubate tubes for 10 min at 20°C–22°C.
Centrifuge tubes at 1,000 × g for 1 min to collect gel pieces in the bottom of the tube.
Discard the supernatant.
Visually inspect the gel to ensure absence of acetonitrile along with the gel.
If necessary, remove remaining traces of acetonitrile by subjecting the gels to brief vacuum centrifugation up to 10 min.
Add 100 μL of Trypsin Peptide Digestion Solution to each sample.
Incubate on ice or in the fridge at 4°C for 30 min to allow absorption of the solution into the gel.
Ensure all gel pieces are completely submerged in the Trypsin Peptide Digestion Solution.
Incubate the gel pieces for 16 hours at 37°C in a heating block covered with aluminum foil to maintain uniform temperature.
Remove samples from the heat block and chill on ice.
Centrifuge samples at 1,000 × g for 1 minute.
Transfer the supernatant containing peptides to a fresh Protein LoBind tube.
Add an additional 100 μL of Peptide Extraction Buffer to the gel pieces.
Incubate the gel pieces with the buffer for 15 minutes at 37°C in a heating block covered with aluminum foil.
Centrifuge samples at 1,000 × g for 1 minute.
Pool supernatants together from previous and current extractions.
Dry the final combined sample at step 5o in a SpeedVac vacuum concentrator at 45°C.
Resuspend each dried peptide sample in 105 μL of 200 mM HEPES (pH 8.8).
Vortex the samples for 10 seconds.
Spin down the samples at 1,000 × g for 1 minute.
Measure the peptide concentration using the PierceTM Quantitative Colorimetric Peptide Assay.
Aliquot 100 μg peptide of each sample into fresh Protein LoBind tubes for labeling in a 10-plex TMT reaction.
Equalize all sample volumes to that of the largest sample volume through addition of 200 mM HEPES (pH 8.8).
Prepare TMT 10-plex Isobaric Label Reagents.
Add 42 μL of anhydrous acetonitrile to each 0.8 mg TMT label vial immediately before use.
Vortex the TMT label vials for 5 minutes and centrifuge at 1,000 g for 1 minute.
Add a different TMT Label to each respective peptide sample (up to 10 samples).
Incubate the labeled samples at 20°C–22°C for 1 hour with occasional vortexing.
Quench excess TMT label by adding 8 μL of TMT Reaction Quenching Solution to each sample.
Vortex each quenched sample for 10 seconds.
Incubate at 20°C–22°C for 15 min.
Perform TMT Label Check.
Create a small scale pooled sample.
Combine approximately 1 μg (2 μL) of each sample into a single fresh Protein LoBind tube.
Vacuum dry the combined sample.
Desalt the combined sample via the SDB Stage-tip clean up procedure using Empore™ SDB SPE Disks.
Dry the desalted sample.
Reconstitute the small scale pooled sample in LC-MS Loading Buffer.
Analyze approximately 1 μg of peptide mixture on the Orbitrap mass spectrometer.
Use the resulting data file (.raw format) for performing a database search by MaxQuant.
Calculate the total TMT reporter ion intensity for each individual sample in the small scale pooled sample.
Calculate the volume of each TMT labeled peptide sample required to generate the large scale pooled sample based on equal levels of total TMT reporter ion intensity.
Create a large scale pooled sample by combining the samples using calculated volumes.
Store the combined sample at 4°C until Label Check is complete.
Dry the final combined sample in a SpeedVac vacuum concentrator.
Pause point: Store the TMT labeled, dried peptides at −20°C or −80°C for up to 6 weeks until further processing.
Desalt TMT labeled peptides using a Sep-Pak Light C18 cartridge.
Resuspend the dried TMT labeled peptide sample in a solution.
Add 1 mL of Sep-Pak Wash Solution to the resuspended sample.
Vortex rigorously for 1 minute.
Centrifuge at 1,000 g for 1 minute.
Check that peptides are fully resuspended and collect total volume at bottom of tube.
Repeat steps if necessary to ensure complete resuspension.
Assemble the Sep-Pak Light C18 cartridge on the vacuum manifold.
Attach a 5 mL collection tube under the Sep-Pak Light C18 cartridge.
Connect the entire assembly to a vacuum line.
Wash the Sep-Pak with 100% methanol (HPLC grade).
Wear appropriate protective gear for handling methanol, including lab coat, gloves, eye protection, and goggles.
Wash the Sep-Pak Light C18 cartridge with 1 mL of Sep-Pak Elution Solution.
Pass the Sep-Pak Elution Solution through the Sep-Pak Light C18 cartridge using a suction pump.
Wash the Sep-Pak Light C18 cartridge with 1 mL of Sep-Pak Wash Solution to equilibrate the column.
Repeat the equilibration procedure twice more to remove all traces of organic solvent.
Place a fresh collection tube under the equilibrated Sep-Pak Light C18 cartridge for flow-through collection.
Fill the Sep-Pak Light C18 cartridge with the sample and let it pass through at approximately 0.5 mL/min.
Wash the Sep-Pak Light C18 cartridge with 1 mL of Sep-Pak Wash Solution to complete the procedure.
Elute peptides into a fresh 1.5 mL tube with 1 mL of Sep-Pak Elution Solution.
Dry peptides in a vacuum centrifuge.
Store desalted, TMT labeled peptides at -80°C if required.
Subject the TMT labeled peptide sample to high pH reverse phase fractionation.
Use an LC system with a fraction collector for high pH fractionation.
Alternatively, use centrifugal high pH columns for fractionation.
Reconstitute sample in 600 μL of HpH Mobile Phase A Solution.
Vigorously vortex the reconstituted sample.
Inject the sample onto the Zorbax 300 Extend-C18 column.
Separate peptides into a total of 96 fractions using an Agilent 1260 HPLC system equipped with quaternary pump, degasser, and Multi-Wavelength Detector (set at 210, 214, and 280-nm wavelength).
Elute the peptides off the column using a gradient of HpH Mobile Phase B Solution.
Operate the elution process at a flow rate of 0.3 mL/min according to the specified table.

Collect the eluate into a 96-well plate using the fraction collector, collecting fractions for 2 minutes each during the first 16 minutes and then 1 minute per fraction until the end of the program at 100 minutes.
Concatenate the collected 96 well fractions into 20 final fractions based on the pattern indicated in Table 2.
Pool peptides from the wells indicated with the same number as specified in the table.
Prepare sample -3 by pooling Ai, Bi, Ci, and Di.
Adjust fractionation control settings and concatenation pattern based on LC chromatogram features.
Collect fractions -3 to -1 (first 14 fractions) to capture the void volume of the column until unbound material is washed out.
Collect subsequent fractions for peptides eluting from the column until the end of the gradient run.
Ensure collection times and windows are adjusted according to individual instrument conditions, including void volume and available collection volume.
Place collected samples into an evaporative concentrator.
Concentrate under vacuum at 45°C to dryness.
Store dried peptide samples at -80°C for up to 2 months.
Reconstitute each of the peptide fractions.
Add 6 μL of LC-MS Loading Buffer to each fraction.
Vortex for 10–30 seconds.
Sonicate for 2–5 minutes.
Centrifuge the samples at 10,000 × g for 2 minutes at 20°C–22°C.
Transfer the supernatant into vials compatible with the liquid chromatography system.
Store TMT labeled samples in MS loading buffer at appropriate temperatures based on storage duration.
Place samples in the auto-sampler system maintained between 4°C–8°C.
Set column heater temperature to 35°C and apply a voltage of 1.9 kV to the nano-LC electrospray ionization source.
Inject each sample onto the peptide trap column.
Wash the peptide trap column with 15 μL LC-MS Mobile Phase A Solution for 10 minutes.
Switch the valve in-line with the column.
Elute peptides from the peptide-trap into the analytical column using a linear gradient of LC-MS Mobile Phase B Solution over 120 minutes, including elution, wash, and re-equilibration phases.
Analyze LC eluent on a Quadrupole-Orbitrap mass-spectrometer (Q Exactive HF-X, Thermo Fisher Scientific) using a MS2-based TMT method.
Analyze raw data files using MaxQuant (Version 1.6.10.43 or above).
Specify parameters for searching TMT proteomics data on MaxQuant software.
Set recommended settings to enhance identification and quantification of proteins.
Apply isobaric match between run (MBR) options in the latest version of MaxQuant for enhanced quantitative depth.
Use alternative software such as Proteome Discoverer, MSFragger, or others if necessary.
Input the TMT kit lot specific reporter ion isotopic distribution correction factors to account for natural carbon isotopes (+1, +2) and incomplete stable isotope incorporation (-1, -2).
Normalize TMT quantitation data by total abundance.
Sum the total ion intensities for each channel.
Conduct t-tests between target protein IP sample groups using normalized data triplicates.
Consider differences between groups with p < 0.05 as biologically significant.
Consider differences with a fold-change of 1.5 as biologically significant.
Conduct Gene Ontology enrichment analysis on lists of differentially expressed proteins.
Consider interacting pathways that may be overrepresented in the initial data.
